children: Indian government bonds inched higher on Wednesday after the previous session's rout as investors awaited the Federal Reserve's policy decision for cues on global yields and the rate outlook.
The benchmark 6.94% 2036 bond (IN069436G=CC) yielded 7.0582% at 12:45 p.m. IST, down 1.5 basis points from Tuesday's four-month closing high.
Muted early trade gave way to some buying as traders said they covered short positions ahead of the Fed decision, and receiving in the overnight indexed swap market aided sentiment.
Interest-rate futures now imply a more than 90% chance of a Fed hike later on Wednesday, up from about 60% a week ago, CME FedWatch tool showed.
The repricing has come in the wake of Brent crude climbing towards $110 a barrel, amplifying inflation concerns and pushing U.S. yields to multi-year highs.
The average 10-year yield across the Group of Seven largest economies reached 4.285%, the highest since mid-2008.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh's credibility is being tested by markets; while a hike could bolster his inflation-fighting credentials, the Fed would need to signal a shallow cycle to avoid an undue tightening of financial conditions, Axis Capital said.
At home, August CPI inflation accelerated to 4.82% from 4.45% in July, hardening bets of an October RBI hike.
The market is also bracing for tighter liquidity as the RBI drains surplus cash through open-market sales, variable-rate reverse repos and sell/buy swaps.
The RBI begins its three-tranche, 1-trillion-rupee ($10.42 billion) bond-sale programme on Thursday, while New Delhi will sell 280 billion rupees of bonds on Friday, adding to supply pressure.
India's OIS rates eased, tracking offshore markets.
The one-year (INR1YMIBROIS=CC) rate fell 2.25 bps to 6.0750%, the two-year (INR2YMIBROIS=CC) rate dropped 2.5 bps to 6.31%, and the five-year (INR5YMIBROIS=CC) rate eased 2.75 bps to 6.6375%.
